title: Former SpaceX engineers are building a robotic factory for automating steel parts manufacturing
summary: Three former SpaceX engineers have founded 1872, a startup aimed at automating steel fabrication using AI-driven software and robotics. The company focuses on producing steel skids for AI data centers and modular nuclear reactors, addressing labor shortages in welding-intensive industries. Their approach combines robotic welding, AI-driven manufacturing planning, and autonomous factory orchestration to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
key_points: 1872, founded by former SpaceX engineers, is developing a robotic factory to automate steel parts manufacturing, targeting critical infrastructure components like steel skids.
The startup aims to address a growing skilled labor shortage in the U.S., particularly in welding, which is critical for building AI data centers, semiconductor fabs, and other infrastructure.
The company leverages AI-driven software (dubbed 'Architect') to plan and schedule manufacturing processes, while a 'Conductor' system orchestrates robotic operations on the factory floor.
Robotic welding, in partnership with Path Robotics, achieves higher efficiency (70% arc-on time) compared to human welders (10-12% arc-on time), reducing costs by up to 85%.
1872 has raised $15 million in seed funding to build its first factory, develop automation software/hardware, and aims to expand beyond steel skids to structural frames and enclosures.
The founders bring experience from SpaceX, where they used intelligent software to rapidly iterate and manufacture rocket engines, a model they are applying to steel fabrication.
